title: Our Story — Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools
description: The Director's message, the founding story behind Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools, our seal, and our Mission, Vision & the CLEVER Standard.
body: Director's Message Zakariya Olanrewaju Anofi B.Sc. Applied Accounting (Oxford Brookes University) · M.Sc. Financial Management (Edinburgh Business School, Heriot-Watt University) · FCCA (UK) · FCA (ICAN) · Doctoral Candidate, Edgewood University, Madison, Wisconsin My name is Zakariya Olanrewaju Anofi, and I am delighted to welcome you to the official home of Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools — the best hybrid, Islamic and secular, school in Lagos, Nigeria, located in Ikorodu. As Director, I am deeply committed to ensuring that every student receives the highest quality education in a nurturing, safe, and inclusive environment. My over two decades of work experience span banking, insurance, oil & gas, and consulting, with a bias for corporate reporting, taxation management, revenue generation, financial and business advisory, governance, and leadership. My passion for education informed my decision to invest in the creation of institutions whose sole motive is to impart knowledge to the populace. Our schools are open to Muslims and non-Muslims, males and females. At SULTAN, our dedicated team of educators are passionate about equipping students with the skills, knowledge, and values they need to succeed in an ever-changing business and technology world. Whether you are a prospective student, a current parent, or an alumni member, we are here to support and guide you. Our Story A Legacy Named in Honour of a Father Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools was founded by Zakariya Olanrewaju Anofi, a professional accountant and educationist, and was officially registered in December 2017. The school takes its name from the founder's late father, Anofi Aliu Akano — a clerk at the Nigerian Ports Authority whose own education was limited, but who was determined that his children would have the opportunities he didn't. Building the school became a way to honour that legacy after his father's passing, during a period when the founder and his younger brother were serving the nation during their NYSC year. The idea took shape years earlier, during Lagos Governor Babatunde Fashola's administration, and was carried through with the encouragement of the founder's mentor, Governor Seyi Makinde, his brother Lukman Olajide Anofi, and others. Rooted in the Imowonla community in Ikorodu, the school has grown into a byword for what focused, values-led education can do for an underserved area — extending its reach through free community lectures, humanitarian relief during the COVID-19 lockdown, and infrastructure support such as road maintenance and community electrification. Scholarly Ties Abroad SULTAN's Islamic and Qur'anic programme is grounded in real scholarly relationships, not built in isolation — visits like this one connect the school to the wider community of Islamic scholarship its curriculum draws on. Source: independent reporting by Punch Newspapers, August 2023. Every Quadrant Tells Part of the Story Crescent & Star Faith as the compass of everything taught here. title: Qur'an College — Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools
description: A 24-to-36 month day & boarding programme in full Qur'an memorisation, Qur'anic sciences, and Arabiyyah, culminating in Ijazaat.
body: School IV of IV Sultan Hanafi Qur'an College IV — Day & Boarding · 24–36 Month Programme Qur'an College Established to provide a platform where students from all walks of life spend an average of 24 to 36 months completing memorisation of the Qur'an, alongside the science of the Qur'an, Arabiyyah language, and other Islamic knowledge and good morals — culminating in standard Ijazaat (licences/certifications) upon completion, under Principal Shaykh Ahmad Ibrahim. Most Qur'an College students board on campus for the duration of the programme — see the Boarding Facility chapter for eligibility and arrangements. The Hifz Journey Stage 1 Memorisation & Muraja'ah New memorisation paired with scheduled revision; a weekly check verifies retention. → Stage 2 Progression Through the 30 Juz' Pace-based, not time-based, across the 24–36 month programme. → Stage 3 Completion Standard All 30 Juz' memorised, retention verified, Tajweed confirmed. → Stage 4 Ijazah Examination The Principal puts the student forward for examination by named scholars. → Stage 5 Ijazah Granted Certified, signed, and permanently recorded in the register. Governed by the Hifz Regulations and Ijazah Governance Framework . title: The Digital Campus — Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools
description: Parent Portal, Student Portal, Staff Identity, Founder Dashboard, and more — one shared set of digital systems serving all four institutions.
body: Shared Infrastructure The Digital Campus A single set of digital systems serving families, students, and staff across all four institutions — not a fifth school, a shared platform every institution draws on. Every system below is real and live today; nothing here is a mockup. 0 Institutions Served 0 Portal Roles For Families Parent Portal Parent Portal A secure account for every guardian: submit and track an admissions enquiry, view your child's attendance, term results and fee status, receive school notifications, and complete a full institutional identity profile. Protected by email verification and one-time-code sign-in on new devices. Sign in to the Parent Portal → Student Portal Student Portal Issued by the school once a student is enrolled — attendance, transcript preview, and fee status, plus a real Hifz & Ijazah tracker for Qur'an College students: current stage of the school's own 5-stage Hifz Journey, a Juz'-by-Juz' progress grid, and any granted Ijazah record. Sign in to the Student Portal → For Staff Staff Identity & Permission Engine Staff Identity & Permission Engine Every staff member's own directory record — office, institution, reporting line, and roles — with access driven by a data-defined Permission Engine built directly from the school's own Role & Permission Matrix, plus a delegation system for temporary, time-bound authority when a colleague is away. Registrar's Office Registrar's Office The system of record for a student's real academic life-cycle — promotions, transfers, withdrawals, graduations, and certificate issuance — each event permanently timestamped, never silently overwritten. Founder Dashboard Founder Dashboard A read-only, institution-wide aggregate for executive leadership — student counts by status and institution, attendance and fee summaries, and Qur'an College Hifz/Ijazah statistics — reporting plainly where a figure (such as consolidated revenue or a staff headcount) isn't available yet, rather than estimating. For Everyone Notice & Announcements Archive Notice & Announcements Archive A public, dated archive of school-wide notices, with a site-wide ribbon surfacing the newest ones as they're published — see the full archive . Morning & Evening Adhkār Centre Morning & Evening Adhkār Centre A full daily remembrance programme — Qur'an and authenticated Hadith texts with translation, transliteration, and sourcing, a built-in Tasbih counter, and family streak-tracking inside the Parent Portal — see the Adhkār Centre . Personalisation Centre Personalisation Centre Site-wide reading and notification preferences for signed-in guardians — theme, text density, prayer-time-aware reminders, and a self-service data export, available from every page. title: Morning & Evening Adhkār — Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools
description: The Morning & Evening Adhkār Centre — Qur'an and authenticated Hadith remembrances with Arabic text, translation, transliteration, and references.
body: Islamic Spiritual Life Morning & Evening Adhkār A daily litany of remembrance from the Qur'an and the authenticated Sunnah, expanded here into a full spiritual companion — prayer-time adhkār, protection, forgiveness, travel, sleep and waking, and the blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ — with a smart counter that stops at each dhikr's prescribed count, Arabic recitation you can follow along with, and a session that adapts to however much time you have. A note on sources: these adhkār follow the well-established "Ḥiṣn al-Muslim" tradition used across Islamic scholarship — Qur'an verses and hadith-authenticated supplications, not a single website's compilation. References are given for every entry so they can be checked against the original sources. This is not a substitute for guidance from the school's own Qur'an College and Islamic & Arabic Studies scholars. {{ADHKAR_STATIC}}

title: Admission — Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools
description: A twelve-stage admission process, the documents required, and how to enrol your ward at Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools.
body: Admission Ready to Start Your Journey A guided, seven-step digital admission journey — from creating your account to your child's enrolment — running on our own Parent Portal and Registrar's Office today. 01 Register Account Create your free Parent Portal account. → 02 Complete Profile Add your details and your child's information. → 03 Admission Application Submit the online admissions application. → 04 Verification Confirm your email with a one-time code or link. → 05 Review Our admissions office reviews your application. → 06 Offer Receive your admission decision in the portal. → 07 Enrolment The Registrar's Office confirms enrolment and class placement. Register / Login → Start Admission Application Prefer to talk to someone first? Reach our admissions office directly. Enquire on WhatsApp Call the Admissions Office Email an Enquiry The Full Operational Process, Stage by Stage The digital journey above runs inside the Parent Portal; the twelve stages below are the fuller operational detail behind it — entrance assessment, fee payment, and the physical documents each learner's file requires. Enquiries Potential parents/guardians approach the school authority. Administrative Office Relevant personnel attend to enquiries and provide guidance. Admission Form Pay for and submit the form with required documents. Contact Details Provide contact information for further communication. Entrance Exam Student sits for the entrance examination, test, and interview. Result Notification Parent/guardian notified of the result for further processing. Admission Offer Offered into the qualifying class based on performance. Fee Payment Pay tuition and other fees upon receipt of admission notice. Admission Letter Issued with a unique number used throughout the learner's stay. Class Acceptance Ticket Received to access the relevant class. Start of Classes Classes begin upon presentation of the access ticket. Settling In The learner enjoys our modern educational infrastructure. title: School Policies — Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools
description: Assessment, Anti-Bullying, Career, Dress Code, Equal Opportunity, First Aid, Health & Safety, Visitors, and Complaint policies, each prepared, reviewed, and approved by named office-holders.
body: Governance School Policies Every policy below is prepared by the VP Administration, reviewed by the Principal, and approved by the CEO, with a scheduled annual review. Print / Download as PDF 0 Published Policies 0 Governance Categories 0 Sections per Policy 0 School Founded Governance GV-01 Constitution & Governance Charter ❧ Policy Information Field Value Policy Code GV-01 Version 2.0 Policy Owner Board of Trustees Approval Authority Board of Trustees Review Cycle Biennial Introduction & Purpose This Charter states, in one place, what kind of institution SULTAN is, who governs it, and what each level of authority may and may not decide alone — the highest document in SULTAN's governance library, which every other policy sits beneath. Institutional Identity & Philosophy SULTAN is a single institution operating four distinct schools under one Board of Trustees and one Executive Management Team — not four independently governed schools sharing a brand. Authority flows from the Board downward through clearly delegated channels; Islamic scholarship and secular educational leadership sit together in the Executive Management Team by design, a structural strength rather than something to flatten into a single generic role. Authority Structure The Board approves this Charter, all Tier 1 governance documents, and appoints the CEO. The CEO directs day-to-day operation across all four institutions. Each institution's Principal or Head Teacher holds academic and disciplinary authority within their institution, but may not adopt a policy that conflicts with a Board-approved document across all four institutions. Continuity & Governance Gaps When a named authority-role holder leaves, their authority passes to a confirmed successor or, until then, to their immediate superior — it never lapses or transfers informally. Where a role this Charter assumes is filled has no named holder (such as the Designated Safeguarding Lead today), that gap is tracked and reported to the Board until resolved, rather than left as a silent assumption. Conclusion This Charter does not establish SULTAN's legal corporate form, which requires confirmation from the school's own legal and corporate records, not an assumption made here. Retrofitted from the original v1.0 draft to SULTAN's full 13-section institutional standard (Policy Information, structured sign-off, cross-referenced governance detail). Prepared by Board of Trustees Reviewed by Executive Management Team Approved by Board of Trustees (pending) Next review Upon adoption Academic AC-01 Assessment Policy ❧ Introduction At SULTAN, assessment is the process by which the quantity and quality of teaching and learning are measured through various techniques, and organised into interpretable forms across a number of variables. Objectives Evaluate teaching and learning practice against specific objectives. Give learners regular performance feedback and ownership of their learning. Give parents a clear idea of progress needed. Benchmark against local and national standards. Identify whole-school professional development needs. Ensure underperforming groups are identified for intervention. Enable educators to plan support to fill knowledge gaps. Uphold the school's high expectations and standards. Report clear information to management and the board of governors. Integrate assessment into planning and teaching. Forms & Techniques Forms: Diagnostic, Formative, Summative. Techniques: Oral questions, classwork, assignments, quizzes, project, test (POP/CBT), exams (POP/CBT). Feedback Learners get constant feedback. Parents receive broad sheets and oral feedback on Open Day each half term. Report cards issued at the end of every term. Report Card Components Learner's individual information and attendance record. Continuous Assessment (CA) score — 40 marks; Examination score — 60 marks; Total — 100 marks per term. Cumulative 200 at 2nd term, 300 at 3rd term; class average. Grading Scale Score Grade Interpr

title: Online Learning Courses — Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools
description: What digital learning already exists at SHRS today, and what is genuinely being planned.
body: Digital Learning Online Learning Courses A self-paced online course platform is not built yet — this page says so plainly rather than listing courses that don't exist. Here's what's actually real today, and what's genuinely being planned. What Already Exists The Adhkār Centre A full daily-remembrance app — Smart Tasbih Counter, Arabic recitation with text-to-speech, streaks, and achievements — already live and free to use. See the Adhkār Centre . The Digital Campus A real Parent Portal, Student Portal, and Founder Dashboard already serve real families today. See the Digital Campus . Curriculum Pages Every school's real curriculum, subjects, and learning model is documented on its own page — see Academics . What's In Development No self-paced video course, quiz engine, or certificate system has been built or scheduled yet. Rather than invent course titles or a launch date no one has committed to, this section will be replaced with real content once a course actually ships. In Development Self-Paced Course Platform A platform for structured, self-paced lessons — potentially starting with Qur'an memorisation support and Arabic language basics — is a genuine idea under consideration, not yet a funded or scheduled project.

title: Digital Qur'an Centre — Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools
description: What's real today toward a daily Qur'an companion, and the legally-clean path for the full Madinah-style reader.
body: Digital Qur'an Centre A Daily Qur'an Companion Our goal for this space: a student, parent, teacher, or ḥāfiẓ should be able to use SHRS as a daily Qur'an companion — not just a page of links. Here's exactly what that means today, and what a proper build requires next. The reader below is a first working draft, pending scholarly verification. Its Arabic text was transcribed by an AI from memory, not fetched from a licensed source (this environment cannot reach one — see below), and has not yet been checked against a printed Mushaf. The school has asked for this best-effort version and taken responsibility for verifying every ayah before it is treated as authoritative. Please do not rely on it for worship or teaching until that review is complete. Reader — Al-Fātiḥah & Surahs 93–114 The opening surah, plus the last block of the Qur'an — the portion most Muslim children memorise first and the one recited most often in daily prayer. The full 604-page Mushaf, verse-by-verse audio, and Hifz repeat-loop tools are a later phase (see below for why). What's Real Today, Beyond the Reader The Adhkār Centre Morning & Evening Adhkār with a Smart Tasbih Counter, Arabic recitation read aloud via text-to-speech, personal streaks, and achievement badges — fully built and live. See the Adhkār Centre . Qur'an College's Real Hifz Tracking Enrolled Qur'an College students already have a genuine Hifz & Ijazah tracker — per-juz' memorisation status, muraja'ah notes, and Ijazah progress — visible to their guardian in the Parent Portal. See Qur'an College and the Digital Campus . Today's Wird, on the Homepage A daily "Today's Adhkār" and "Today's Islamic Reminder" (a well-established verse or hadith, with its citation) greet every visitor on the homepage. See Today's Wird . Why the Reader Above Is Scoped and Unverified, and What Finishing It Needs Building the reader properly — the full 604-page Mushaf, verse-by-verse audio, and Hifz repeat-loop tools — means the verse text and audio need to come from a real, licensed data source fetched programmatically, then be checked by qualified reviewers before anyone relies on them. The version above is a deliberately smaller first step: 23 short, commonly-recited surahs, transcribed by AI at the school's explicit request and awaiting that same scholarly check. Research into what the fuller, licensed build needs: Researched Qur'an Text Tanzil Project 's Uthmani text is available under Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 — verbatim copying and redistribution is permitted with attribution and a link back to tanzil.net. This is the standard source most Qur'an apps use. Researched Madinah-Style Typesetting The King Fahd Glorious Qur'an Printing Complex's own KFGQPC Uthmanic Script font is freely distributed for non-commercial typesetting use — this is how to get an authentic Madinah-Mushaf look. The scanned photographic pages of the actual Madinah Mushaf are a separate matter and are not under a comparably clear open licence — reproducing those specific page images would need direct written permission from the Complex first. Researched Recitation Audio Reciter audio hosted on sites like EveryAyah.com is generally under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial terms — usable for a non-commercial educational site like this one, with attribution, but each reciter's exact terms should be re-checked individually before enabling their voice specifically. Blocked, Not Skipped What Stopped This Build Going Further Today This working session has no outbound network access to Qur'an text/audio APIs (a sandboxing restriction, confirmed by testing), so the actual verse data for the fuller Mushaf could not be fetched from Tanzil and verified here, and audio recitation isn't wired in at all.
